newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- MONOPOLIES REFERRAL FOR FERRY MERGER

A planned merger between two of the largest ferry operators on the English Channel has been put on hold after the government announced it was referring the proposal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. Britain's P&O and the Swedish company Stena Line had hoped their merger would lead to annual cost savings of 75 million stg. Now the companies may not be able to merge their Channel operations in time for the busy Easter and summer period next year.
-- DEALING ROOMS SABOTAGED BY HK REUTERS TECHNICIAN

A disgruntled computer technician at Reuters in Hong Kong has caused the financial information company deep embarrassment by sabotaging the dealing room systems of five of the company's investment bank clients.
-- OSTRICH INVESTORS GET SHARE OFFER WITH A KICK

Investors who bought birds in the Ostrich Farming Corp venture that was closed down in April are to be offered shares for their birds in the world's first ostrich-for-equity swap. The venture was closed by the Department of Trade and Industry and is being investigated by the Serious Fraud Office, as its liquidators seek to trace 3.75 million stg in assets. The offer to the OFC investors is being made by a new company, Belautruche, which has links with Europe's largest ostrich farming operation based in southern Belgium.
-- EU TO CHALLENGE US RULES ON TEXTILES

The European Union is to investigate recent changes in US customs rules for textiles and clothing imports following complaints by the Italian silk scarf industry. The investigation will take place under the EU's trade barriers regulation, which was introduced earlier this year to ensure that other countries provide fair market access for European exporter. The EU claims that the US measures, which have also been attacked by other international exporters, could also affect exports of British hats, German soft furnishings and Austrian cotton goods.
-- DEFENCE DEAL OPENS DOOR TO GULF SALES

Britain has finally signed a mutual defence agreement with the United Arab Emirates, clearing the way for future defence export sales from UK companies to the Gulf state. The UAE has always maintained it would only buy arms from countries that agreed to come its aid should the Gulf state be attacked. The US and France signed defence deals with the UAE several years ago, and French and American companies have since won contracts worth over $10 billion.
-- BRITISH GAS ANNOUNCES 294 MILLION STG WRITE-OFF

British Gas has reported third quarter net losses of 364 million stg on an historic cost basis, compared to losses of 181 million stg for the same period last year. The losses were deepened by an exceptional charge of 294 million stg for provision against potential losses on long-term supply contracts. The provision relates to the 'take-or-pay' contracts the company agreed with 36 North Sea gas suppliers when the price of gas was much higher. British Gas is currently renegotiating the contracts with the suppliers, with one investment bank - SBC Warburg WSG.L - estimating the cost of the contracts to the group at some 1.3 million stg.
-- SOUTHERN UTILITY PUTS ACQUISITION ON HOLD

Kent-based regional electricity company Southern Electric has announced it is to postpone acquisition plans and that it plans to return up to 10 percent of the company's share capital to shareholders in a package estimated by analysts to be worth about 180 million stg -- or about 70p a share. The announcement came as Southern reported half-year pre-tax profits of 112.2 million stg, a fall of 5.5 percent on the same period last year. The company said it has revised plans for growth through acquisition because of the current 'changing political and regulatory environment' in Britain.
-- DE BENEDETTI WARNS OF 'CRISIS' AT OLIVETTI

Carlo De Benedetti, the former chairman of troubled Italian electronics, computers and telecoms group Olivetti, has said mismanagement of the current 'difficult but manageable' situation could turn into 'a crisis without means of exit'. De Benedetti was speaking before parliamentary deputies at a hearing in Italy's lower house into events at the company. Whilse admitting the group currently 'lacks credibility', he defended the decision to focus on telecommunications and systems and services and plans to sell-off the loss-making PC division.
-- WICKES TO APPOINT NEW CHIEF

Builders' merchant group Wickes is to announce the appointment of Bill Grimsey, currently the managing director of the core trading company Wickes Building Supplies, as new chief executive. The news comes as it was revealed that former senior managers at Wickes are under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office following irregularities in accounting. Wickes hopes to launch a 30 million stg rights issue to rebuild the company's balance sheet following the scandal, a move that would clear the way for the suspension of shares in Wickes to be lifted.
-- UTD UTILITIES AIMS AT DEREGULATED MARKET

United Utilities has announced plans to launch a new company next year to compete in the deregulated UK energy market after 1998. United, a combined water and electricity group, is said to be in 'deep discussions' with other gas and electricity suppliers about the proposed venture, which is likely to involve a tie-up with another regional electricity supplier. The announcement came as United reported a 34 percent increase in interim pre-tax profits to 223.9 million stg for the six months to September 30.
